study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Meijer et al., Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Toward Understanding Autism Heterogeneity: Identifying Clinical Subgroups and Neuroanatomical Deviations

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study combined ABIDE I (17 sites, 1112 participants: 539 autism, 573 NAI) and ABIDE II (19 sites, 1114 participants: 521 autism, 593 NAI). Sites with same/highly similar imaging protocols were merged across ABIDE I and II (KKI, NYU, SDSU, UCLA_1). After exclusions for primary (males-only) normative modeling analysis: 690 autistic and 744 NAI, age 5-64 years.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We combined the ABIDE repositories I (Di Martino et al., 2014) and II (Di Martino et al., 2017). ABIDE I includes a total of 1,112 participants (539 autism, 573 NAI) from 17 different sites, and ABIDE II includes 1,114 participants (521 autism, 593 NAI) from 19 different sites."

answer.ABIDE (I+II): normative model training (90% of NAI), normative model testing (remaining 10% of NAI + all autistic individuals), clinical subgroup clustering, and SVM classification

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The combined ABIDE I+II dataset served multiple purposes: (1) Model-based clustering on ADOS-G subscores to identify clinical subgroups in autistic individuals (N autism=499); (2) Normative modeling on CT and subcortical ROIs using warped likelihood BLR, with 90% NAI as training set and 10% NAI + all autistic individuals as test set (N autism=690, N NAI=744 for males-only primary analysis); (3) SVM classification to test biological separability of subgroups.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The data set was split into a training set consisting of 90% of NAI and a test set consisting of all autistic individuals and the remaining 10% of NAI. We ensured that age, FIQ, and site were evenly distributed across the training and test sets."

model-1.model-name: CT and subcortical volume normative model (males only)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: One normative model was constructed (separately for each of 148 CT ROIs and 23 subcortical ROIs but using the same dataset split). The total NAI sample for the males-only primary normative modeling analysis was 744. The training set consisted of 90% of NAI (744 * 0.9 = 669.6, approximately 670), and the test set consisted of the remaining 10% of NAI (approximately 74) plus all 690 autistic individuals. A supplementary analysis including both sexes used 972 NAI (744 males + 228 females).
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "This resulted in a sample of 690 autistic and 744 NAI between 5 and 64 years who were included in the normative modeling analysis" ... "The data set was split into a training set consisting of 90% of NAI and a test set consisting of all autistic individuals and the remaining 10% of NAI."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Table 1 provides demographics for NAI (N=886) before analyses-specific exclusion criteria: M=16.58, SD=8.96, Range=5.9-64. This is the full male+female pre-exclusion sample. The normative model used 744 NAI (males only, after exclusions), for which separate age statistics are not provided. The overall-phase values are inferred from the pre-exclusion NAI demographics in Table 1 and may not precisely reflect the 744 males used. The train-phase (90% of NAI) age statistics are not separately reported. The authors state they ensured age was evenly distributed across train and test sets.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Primary analyses were conducted in males only due to limited sample size of females (N autism=130, N NAI=280 before exclusion). Therefore, the normative model's NAI sample of 744 consisted entirely of males. The 90% training split (approximately 670) and 10% test split (approximately 74) were also all males. A supplementary normative model including both sexes used 972 NAI (744 males, 228 females) with sex as an additional covariate.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "For primary analyses, we excluded females due to scarce availability and autistic individuals whose ADOS-Generic (ADOS-G) had not been administered by research-reliable personnel" ... "primary analyses were conducted in males only due to limited sample size of females (N autism = 130, N NAI = 280)."
